 PostgreSQL is authoritative for durable governance configuration and usage ledger; Redis or a proven equivalent can own hot atomic counters, leases, breaker observations and short-lived admission reservations, synchronized by event/version design. Document whether each feature provides strict/leased/best-effort semantics. Replica failures require expiry/fencing and reconciliation. No architecture relies on node affinity to enforce tenant budgets. Concurrency/load tests must exercise race conditions across ≥2 gateway replicas and target the same scoped counters.
 
-ISK-0005 sets the coordination ports every distributed feature uses (single-key atomic operations, leases with fencing tokens, the fencing guard, and the versioned cache), the level each coordinator declares per primitive (`local`, `best_effort`, `leased`, or `strict`), how a feature declares its minimum levels and its `fail_closed` or `degrade` outage behavior, and the start-up check that refuses a feature its deployment cannot serve, in its [coordination contract](../specs/0005-coordination-redis-capability-contracts/contracts/coordination.md). Redis declares `leased` and PostgreSQL `strict`, and only PostgreSQL-issued leases pass the fencing guard.
+ISK-0005 sets the coordination ports every distributed feature uses (single-key atomic operations, leases with fencing tokens, the fencing guard, and the versioned cache), the level each coordinator declares per primitive (`local`, `best_effort`, `leased`, or `strict`), how a feature declares its minimum levels and its `fail_closed` or `degrade` outage behavior, and the start-up check that refuses a feature its deployment cannot serve, in its coordination contract, linked from the Persistence, publication and distributed coordination section of [03](03-domain-and-technical-architecture.md). Redis declares `leased` and PostgreSQL `strict`, and only PostgreSQL-issued leases pass the fencing guard.
 
+ISK-0009 sets the durable internal work handoff that reconciliation and recovery can run on, in its work contract, linked from the same section of [03](03-domain-and-technical-architecture.md): a module enqueues a work item in the same unit of work as its change, and the worker, the control-plane image's `work` command, delivers it at least once, in no order, to one handler that applies its database effects at most once in a unit of the item's scope, fenced by a PostgreSQL-issued lease. It uses no broker, offers no broadcast to every replica, and needs PostgreSQL leases in the worker, whatever coordinator the planes use.
+
 ## Operational controls and diagnostics
 
 Every rejected decision has safe machine-readable reason (`auth_denied`, `model_disallowed`, `quota_exceeded`, `budget_blocked`, `no_healthy_backend`, etc.) with effective scope and correlation ID where disclosure is permitted. Provide preview/simulation of effective policy/routing *configuration* in MVP; rich counterfactual simulations are post-MVP. Telemetry records request count, tokens, estimate provenance, reservations, retries, circuit state, backend selection and error classes with cardinality limitations [12](12-observability-and-nonfunctional-requirements.md).

 - **Status:** Approved.
 - **Context:** ADR-0003 and ADR-0005 require versioned contracts and opaque, owner-scoped resource IDs, and the constitution requires versioned SDK and API surfaces. ADR-0030 gives pre-MVP prereleases no compatibility commitment. No ADR said how IDs are formed, how errors are classified, or how a breaking change to a public contract is caught.
-- **Decision:** A resource ID is `<prefix>_<26 Crockford base32 characters>` holding 128 random bits, with each prefix registered in `Iskender.Core.Contracts` and never reused. Its text has no version marker, and any change to that text form is a break. Every error has a registered, dot-namespaced code and safe message and belongs to one of 13 transport-neutral categories, each with a fixed retry rule. A later spec may add codes, but a new category needs a revision of the contract. The `error-envelope` wire contract never carries credentials, content, or another tenant's identifiers, and is always `withheld` for `not_found`. `Iskender.Core.Contracts`, `Iskender.Providers.Abstractions`, and `Iskender.Policy.Sdk` are versioned as separate contracts, every public type is tagged with its contract and version, and each wire contract has its own version. Until ISK-0086 completes, a break passes only when it is declared in the break record, approved by the Architecture (ADR) owner, and its contract version is incremented. `tests/Iskender.Contracts.Compatibility.Tests` compares each change with its merge base on `origin/main` and fails on any other break. The current [public contracts and versioning contract](../specs/0002-public-contracts-versioning-discipline/contracts/public-contracts-and-versioning.md), first published by ISK-0002, holds the exact registries, rules, and wire formats.

Until ISK-0086 completes, a break passes only when it is declared in the break record, approved by the Architecture (ADR) owner, and its contract version is incremented. `tests/Iskender.Contracts.Compatibility.Tests` compares each change with its merge base on `origin/main` and fails on any other break. The current public contracts and versioning contract, linked from the Interfaces, isolation and portability section of [03](03-domain-and-technical-architecture.md) and first published by ISK-0002, holds the exact registries, rules, and wire formats.
 - **Rationale:** One ID format and one error contract stop each module from inventing its own. Per-contract versions show which contract changed while package versions follow spec numbers under ADR-0030. Declared breaks keep the pre-MVP surface changeable without letting a break go unnoticed.
 - **Consequences / trade-offs:** Any change to a package's public surface, an addition included, increments that contract's version. The harness needs `origin/main` fetched. `.github/CODEOWNERS` requests the owner's review of a declared break, but GitHub does not require it while DEC-20261105-002 holds. A resource ID shows its type through its prefix. ISK-0086 must replace the pre-MVP declared-break rule with its release rule.
 - **References:** [03](03-domain-and-technical-architecture.md), [04](04-technology-stack-and-deployment.md), [07](07-provider-adapters-and-api-compatibility.md), [17](17-master-spec-inventory.md).
